ai.description: This slender, iridescent black snake reaches 40–50 cm. It is distinguished by two prominent yellow lateral stripes and a blunt, rounded tail tip. It belongs to the family Uropeltidae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Melanophidium bilineatum* is uniquely distinguished by the two distinct, continuous yellow or cream-colored lateral stripes running along its otherwise iridescent black body.
ai.habitat: *Melanophidium bilineatum* inhabits the moist, leaf-littered floors of tropical evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 800 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Two-lined Black Earth Snake is a secretive, fossorial species that remains primarily subterranean, emerging to the surface mainly during or after heavy rainfall.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Melanophidium bilineatum* is ovoviviparous, giving birth to a small litter of live young. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Melanophidium bilineatum* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically inhabiting high-elevation forests above 1,000 meters.
